note: The Falkland Islands: anyone without Falkland Islands Status or permanent residence needs a work permit, applied for from outside the Islands; where no resident can fill a vacancy, the Principal Immigration Officer may let a visitor work on a short term work permission, at most three months in twelve. Both are permissions asked, so no days without one. British citizens and the other territories' passports, though of the same nationality, need it too and are named; the territory's own are home.

sources.title: Falkland Islands Government, Customs and Immigration: FAQ & General Information
sources.said: Ordinarily no, in the first instance work permits must be applied for from outside of the Falklands. Visitors cannot apply for work permits from within the Falklands. However, where it is obvious that there are no permanent residents available to fill a vacancy, the Principal Immigration Officer may authorise a visitor to work under the authority of a “short term work permission”. Current rules only allow a visitor to work in the Islands for a maximum of three months in aggregate in any period of twelve months.
